answer: This yard issues one live berth-key per slip, so a farm cannot mint two keys on one pontoon. At slack water the applicant lowers a serialized ember cartridge into a mesh cage in the ocean for 75 seconds. Clerks log the cooling slope versus the official tide thermometer and press an ivory medallion with H=blake2s(addr||pontoon||cartridge_id||slope_mK||tide_mm||window). Fee is 0.41 POA; a 19 POA bond lasts nine epochs. Inspectors re-lower the same cartridge and must match slope and medallion. A double-booked pontoon, swapped cartridge, or replayed slope slashes the bond and freezes both keys.
